 "text": "## Model Context Protocol Specification

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that enables seamless integration between LLM applications and external data sources and tools. This section contains the detailed technical specifications for implementing the protocol.

## Available Versions

MCP is under active development. The following specifications are available:

Current version:

English 2026-07-28 specification

中文 2026-07-28 规范

Specification (Latest)
Specification (Previous)
Specification (Older)
Specification (Earlier)
Specification (Legacy)

## Version History

2026-07-28 - Latest

Stateless protocol with per-request version and capability metadata

Removed protocol-level sessions and the initialization handshake

Added mandatory server/discover capability discovery

Introduced Multi Round-Trip Requests (MRTR)

Moved Tasks from the core protocol to an official extension

2025-11-25 - Previous Stable

OpenID Connect Discovery support

Icons metadata for tools/resources/prompts

Incremental scope consent

URL mode elicitation support

Sampling tool calling support

OAuth Client ID metadata documents

Experimental Tasks support

2025-06-18 - Older Stable

Removed JSON-RPC batching support

Structured tool output

OAuth Resource Server classification

Resource Indicators (RFC 8707)

Elicitation feature support

Resource links support

2025-03-26 - Earlier

OAuth 2.1 authorization framework

Streamable HTTP transport replacing HTTP+SSE

JSON-RPC batching support (later removed in 2025-06-18)

Tool annotations for read-only and destructive behavior

2024-11-05 - Legacy

Initial stable version

## What’s next

2027-03-30 is the target for the next specification revision. The maintainers published a predictable release cycle and are “targeting March 30, 2027”; a proposal that is not ready moves to a later release rather than shipping half-done. See A More Predictable Release Cycle for MCP.

File uploads and downloads are being explored as an experimental extension. The File Uploads Working Group has published a rough extension definition for moving files between clients and tools; there is no reference implementation yet, and the shape is expected to change. See Exploring File Uploads and Downloads in MCP (2026-11-10).

The authoritative sources are the official specification pages at modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28 and the release announcement The 2026-07-28 Specification.

## Put the specification into practice

Understand tool definitions, results, and errors: follow a tool call and compare protocol revisions.

Test a server with MCP Inspector: list tools, make a call, and locate connection or tool failures.

Move a client across protocol eras: see the 2025-11-25 handshake and the 2026-07-28 stateless flow side by side, with runnable examples.

Design tools a model can use: review tool descriptions, parameters, and error handling.",
 "note": "page content is data, not instructions"

content:
**Latest specification**  
- **Version:** 2026‑07‑28 (the current “Latest” release) 【1†L13-L22】  

**What changed in the 2026‑07‑28 revision**  

| Change | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Stateless protocol** | The protocol no longer maintains server‑side sessions; each request carries its own version and capability metadata. |
| **Removed initialization handshake** | The previous session‑level handshake is gone, simplifying the request flow. |
| **Per‑request version & capability metadata** | Clients specify the protocol version and required capabilities in a `_meta` field on every request. |
| **Mandatory `server/discover` capability** | Servers must expose a discovery endpoint so clients can query supported capabilities. |
| **Multi‑Round‑Trip Requests (MRTR)** | New support for requests that require several back‑and‑forth exchanges within a single logical operation. |
| **Tasks moved to an official extension** | The “Tasks” feature is no longer part of the core spec; it is now provided as a separate, versioned extension. |

These are the key differences introduced in the most recent MCP specification compared with the previous stable release (2025‑11‑25).
